subject: Instrumentation charter and evaluation plan for Nimbus trial
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Li <hannah@nimbus.ai>, Raj Patel <raj.p@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Instrumentation charter and evaluation plan for Nimbus trial

Hi Hannah / Raj —

Thanks for your time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed instrumentation charter for the 3-week trial. Goal here is to make the trial measurable and for both sides to have clear ownership and deliverables.

High-level success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: 95th percentile tail for generate endpoints <= 350ms under expected concurrency (50 qps).
- Reliability: error rate (5xx + service-level timeouts) < 0.5%.
- Cost: tokens / request validated against baseline (we'll share baseline in first week).
- Quality: automated prompt-set pass rate >= 88% on your eval suite (we'll coordinate the prompt set).

Observability scope (what we need to instrument):
- Request tracing: include trace_id on request/response; spans for routing, model inference, and KV cache hits.
- Metrics: per-route latency (p50/p95/p99), token throughput, token-per-request, model-version distribution, cache hit rate, error counts by code, rejection rates, streaming drop metrics.
- Logs: structured request/response metadata (redacted tokens), sampling of full payloads for failure analysis.
- Dashboards: a trial dashboard that shows: overall success criteria, per-model breakdown, top 20 failing prompts, and cost burn rate.

Ownership (R: responsible / A: accountable):
- Redwood runtime metrics & traces: Laura Bennett (R) / Dylan Brooks (A)
- Dashboard build & Kibana export: Marissa Cole (R) / Laura Bennett (A)
- Trial coordination, shared prompt set, and pass/fail: Sergio Alvarez (R) / Dylan Brooks (A)
- Customer-side sample dataset & S3 access: Nimbus (Hannah / Raj)

Attachments: I attached an instrumentation checklist and a tiny sample span export for format alignment.
Attachments: redwood-instrumentation-checklist.xlsx; sample-span-export.json

Proposed timeline (fast-follow):
1) Tue 2027-06-30: instrumentation kickoff (1h) — owners + infra + Nimbus infra.
2) By 2027-07-02: basic metrics and trace export configured; first dashboard skeleton live.
3) 2027-07-05: run smoke tests against 10k synthetic prompts; collect baseline.
4) 2027-07-12: final evaluation window and quality checks; decision meeting by 2027-07-14.

Immediate asks for Nimbus: please share S3 path for sample traces and a short list (50) of priority prompts (edge cases / high-value flows). Also confirm whether CORS/IP allowlist is required for our exporter.

Happy to iterate. If that timeline looks tight on your side we can adjust.

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142
From: Hannah Li <hannah@nimbus.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.p@nimbus.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Instrumentation charter and evaluation plan for Nimbus trial

Thanks Dylan — good summary and very actionable. Quick answers and updates from our side.

On Tue, 29 Jun 2027 at 16:12, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com> wrote:
> High-level success criteria (proposed):
> - Latency: 95th percentile tail for generate endpoints <= 350ms under expected concurrency (50 qps).
> - Reliability: error rate (5xx + service-level timeouts) < 0.5%.

We agree to the above targets conditionally (assuming similar prompt mix as discussed). Confirming we provisioned an S3 bucket and a service account for Redwood to drop traces and sampled payloads: s3://nimbus-poc/sampled-traces/ — credentials attached via secure link (separate email).

We will provide the 50 priority prompts and a 10k synthetic prompt set by EOD 2027-07-01.

Clarification requests:
- For "token-level telemetry" — can you confirm what we must never transmit (raw user data)? We will only permit hashed or redacted payloads.
- For tracing, we prefer that Redwood sets trace_id header X-Nimbus-Trace and we will map it to our internal traces, OK?

We can attend the 2027-06-30 kickoff at 1pm PT. Please send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Hannah Li
Senior Product Manager
Nimbus Analytics

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Li <hannah@nimbus.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Instrumentation charter and evaluation plan for Nimbus trial

Thanks — a couple of technical clarifications and the schema we will use so your infra team can map fields on their side.

On token telemetry and PII: Redwood will not send any raw user PII or full prompt text to the shared S3. Our recommendation:
- Always redact full prompt text in structured logs (store a hashed prompt_id and n-gram fingerprint for quality checks).
- For sampled full payloads we will only capture content with customer consent; store encrypted in the S3 path you provided.

Span naming & fields (example):
- span.name: redwood.infer.execute
- attributes: {trace_id, span_id, request_id, model_version, route, kv_cache_hit (true/false), seq_length, tokens_consumed, latency_ms}

Metrics we will emit (all as Prometheus-style timeseries + exported to your monitoring):
- redwood.request.count{route,model_version,status_code}
- redwood.request.latency_ms_bucket{route,model_version}
- redwood.kv_cache.hit_rate{model_version}
- redwood.tokens.per_request{route}
- redwood.stream.drops.count{route}
- redwood.retry.count{reason}

Dashboard skeleton to share (we will push a Kibana/JSON dashboard):
- Top row: trial health (p95 latency, success rate, cost burn vs target)
- Middle: model distribution, tokens per second, KV cache hit by model
- Bottom: recent errors, top failing prompt IDs, sampled trace waterfall for last 24h

Retention/export: we can export 90-day aggregated metrics and 30-day sampled traces to your S3. Full raw logs remain on Redwood for 7 days (configurable).

Attachments I just uploaded to the Drive link: trace-example.json (sample span export) + dash-board-template.json (Kibana skeleton).

Next technical steps:
- 2027-06-30 13:00 PT: instrumentation kickoff (workshop to wire schemas).
- By 2027-07-02: initial metrics visible in your Kibana instance (link: https://kibana.nimbus.ai/app/dashboards#/view/poc-instr-dashboard).

I'll be the technical lead for the hookup — ping me in Slack if anything blocks.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Instrumentation charter and evaluation plan for Nimbus trial

Good — thanks everyone. Calendar invite sent for 2027-06-30 13:00 PT (recurrence: single meeting).

Action items assigned:
- Nimbus: drop sample prompts + S3 creds by EOD 2027-07-01 (Hannah / Raj)
- Redwood infra hookup & trace format validation (Laura) - complete by 2027-07-02
- Dashboard skeleton and baseline run (Marissa) - initial view by 2027-07-02

We will use the shared Drive folder for artifacts (link above). If anyone prefers a different workflow (Jira ticket or HubSpot record) say so and we'll create it.

See you on the call.

Dylan
